blocks.content: Quiz: Why do we use entries.filter(...) instead of finding the index and using splice to remove the entry?
Tap an option below to answer:
Because splice is slower than filter
The reason is immutability and React's behavior, not speed.
The reason is immutability and React's behavior, not speed.
Because filter returns a new array while splice mutates the existing one
React compares state by reference. splice modifies the original array in place, so the reference stays the same and React may not notice the change.
React compares state by reference. splice modifies the original array in place, so the reference stays the same and React may not notice the change.
Because filter is the only way to remove an item in JavaScript
JavaScript also gives you splice. But using it results in a mutating state.
JavaScript also gives you splice. But using it results in a mutating state.
So that the deleted entry stays in memory
The purpose of deleting an entry is to remove it from the memory, not to keep it.
The purpose of deleting an entry is to remove it from the memory, not to keep it.
